_note: Broad literature map (Block 9 §3), reviewed BEFORE any Top-5 selection or backtest. Depth varies deliberately: the 8 families named as Priority Research Areas (§7) and the 5 selected families received a full source review (see docs/BLOCK9_STRATEGY2_DISCOVERY_REPORT.md); the remaining letters received a map-depth pass (grade + rationale + why it was or wasn't advanced) sufficient to justify inclusion/exclusion without pretending to a full deep-dive that wasn't done.

gradeDefinitions.A: Multiple independent studies, long history, different markets, plausible economic explanation.
gradeDefinitions.C: Mixed evidence, decay, or implementation concerns.

families.name: Time-series momentum / trend
families.economicRationaleOrigin: behavioral (underreaction/herding) + institutional (delegated-manager trend chasing)
keyReferences: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), "Time Series Momentum", Journal of Financial Economics
Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (AQR, 2017), "A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing"
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced. Real, well-documented edge, but structurally close to RS3M's own momentum-like rotation (§6 explicitly penalizes 'RS3M with another lookback'). Block 5's Momentum/Trend family and Block 8.3's Family 4 (Cross-Index Rotation) already tested closely related implementations on this project's own universe and both were rejected or downgraded for exactly this redundancy (0.90-0.95 correlation with RS3M). Re-testing trend/momentum on the same 4-ETF universe would not diversify RS3M.

families.name: Cross-sectional momentum
families.economicRationaleOrigin: behavioral (underreaction) + information diffusion
keyReferences: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993), "Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers", Journal of Finance
Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013), "Value and Momentum Everywhere", Journal of Finance
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced. RS3M IS a cross-sectional momentum/relative-strength rotation by construction (§0). Testing this family again on the same SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA universe is definitionally 'RS3M with another ranking' — excluded per §6 without needing a new backtest to know it.

families.name: Short-term reversal
families.economicRationaleOrigin: liquidity provision + market microstructure (overreaction to non-fundamental order flow)
keyReferences: Da, Liu & Schaumburg (2014), "A Closer Look at the Short-Term Return Reversal", Management Science
Lehmann (1990), "Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency", Quarterly Journal of Economics
Nagel (2012), "Evaporating Liquidity", Review of Financial Studies
families.verdict: ADVANCED to Top-5 (#5). Genuinely different time horizon (days, not months) and different mechanism (liquidity/overreaction, not trend-following) from RS3M. Da-Liu-Schaumburg's own finding that costs erode the standard reversal strategy (especially small-cap) is the main falsification risk — this project restricts the test to SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA (large, liquid, low-spread) specifically to address that concern, at the cost of a likely thinner edge than small-cap studies report.

families.name: Overnight / intraday return decomposition
families.economicRationaleOrigin: structural (index-fund/ETF creation flows concentrated near the close) + information diffusion (news arriving overnight) + institutional (overnight risk transfer)
keyReferences: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019), "A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns", Journal of Financial Economics
Hendershott, Livdan & Rösch (2020), "Asset Pricing: A Tale of Night and Day", Journal of Financial Economics
Cliff, Cooper & Gulen (2008), "Return Differences between Trading and Non-Trading Hours" (working paper)
families.verdict: ADVANCED to Top-5 (#1). Strongest, most-replicated, most economically distinct source in this review — see full writeup in the discovery report.

families.name: Volatility risk premium
families.economicRationaleOrigin: risk premium (compensation for insuring against variance/crash risk) + behavioral (overpaying for crash insurance)
keyReferences: Carr & Wu (2009), "Variance Risk Premia", Review of Financial Studies
Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou (2009), "Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia", Review of Financial Studies
Bondarenko (2014), "Why Are Put Options So Expensive?", Quarterly Journal of Finance
families.verdict: ADVANCED to Top-5 (#2), gated on defined-risk implementation only — see tail-risk discussion in the discovery report.

families.name: Defensive / low-beta / low-volatility
families.economicRationaleOrigin: institutional (leverage-constrained investors bid up high-beta names) + behavioral (lottery preference for high-vol stocks)
keyReferences: Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang (2006), "The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns", Journal of Finance
Frazzini & Pedersen (2014), "Betting Against Beta", Journal of Financial Economics
Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011), "Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage", Financial Analysts Journal
families.verdict: ADVANCED to Top-5 (#4).

families.name: Equity seasonality (general, non turn-of-month)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: institutional (tax-loss selling / window dressing) + behavioral
keyReferences: Haugen & Jorion (1996), "The January Effect", Financial Analysts Journal
McLean & Pontiff (2016), "Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?", Journal of Finance
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — folded into letter M below (Turn-of-Month is the specific, better-evidenced seasonal effect this project actually tests). Broader calendar effects (January effect, day-of-week, holiday) are graded lower here: McLean & Pontiff's own post-publication decay finding applies most strongly to exactly this category, and most surviving day-of-week/January patterns are now small enough to be cost-negative on liquid large-cap ETFs.

families.name: Cross-asset signals (rates, VIX, credit, USD, commodities → equity exposure)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: risk premium (credit/vol markets price systemic risk before equities fully reprice) + information diffusion
keyReferences: Gilchrist & Zakrajšek (2012), "Credit Spreads and Business Cycle Fluctuations", American Economic Review
Johnson (2017), "Equity Risk Premia and the VIX Term Structure", working paper (Bauer College of Business / job market paper)
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced this round. Real evidence, but the brief's own instruction (§7.E) to avoid a 40-variable macro model plus the overlap with E (VIX-based) makes this most useful as a future SIMPLE overlay (e.g., a single credit-spread-percentile filter), not a standalone 20-config family this round. Documented for a later, narrower follow-up.

families.name: Market breadth
families.economicRationaleOrigin: information diffusion (breadth reveals participation width that price alone does not) + behavioral (narrow rallies mask distribution)
keyReferences: Zaremba, Kizys, Aharon & Umar (2021), "Herding for Profits: Market Breadth and the Cross-Section of Global Equity Returns", International Review of Financial Analysis
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced this round. Zaremba et al. find breadth adds information beyond simple trend/momentum measures, which is a real, citable result — but per this block's own §7.F warning, breadth risks becoming 'just another filter on RS3M' rather than an independent P&L source, and most freely available US breadth series (advancers/decliners, % above 200dma) are index-provider proprietary or require a paid feed for point-in-time accuracy. Flagged for future work, not this round's 20-config budget.

families.name: Volatility timing (using realized/implied vol to size or time equity exposure)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: risk premium (vol clustering) + institutional (vol-targeting fund flows)
keyReferences: Moreira & Muir (2017), "Volatility-Managed Portfolios", Journal of Finance
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — ALREADY TESTED. This is Block 8.3's Family 1 (Volatility-Managed Equity Exposure): DSR up to 1.0 (the round's strongest standalone result) but 0.79-0.82 correlated with RS3M — downgraded to RESEARCH for exactly the diversification reason this block screens on (§6). No new trial needed; re-testing it would burn budget on an already-answered question.

families.name: Trend + crisis alpha (diversified managed-futures-style trend across asset classes)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: behavioral/institutional (herding, delegated trend-chasing) — the same root cause as A, applied cross-asset for crisis-period diversification
families.expectedCorrelationWithRs3m: MEDIUM (crisis periods LOW, calm periods overlaps with A)
keyReferences: Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (AQR, 2017), "A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing"
Man Group (2015+), "Trend Following: Equity and Bond Crisis Alpha", Man Institute research
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced. Genuinely strong evidence, but its real diversification value (crisis alpha) comes specifically from cross-asset breadth (bonds, commodities, FX futures) that this project's Alpaca-equity/ETF universe cannot access without a futures broker (§7.H). Implemented equity-only, it degenerates back into family A (already excluded for RS3M redundancy). Correctly belongs under a future FUTURES-INFRASTRUCTURE roadmap item, not this round's equity-only budget.

families.name: Gap / overnight effects (opening-auction-specific behavior)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: market microstructure (opening auction price discovery, overnight order imbalance)
keyReferences: Cliff, Cooper & Gulen (2008), "Return Differences between Trading and Non-Trading Hours" (working paper)
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — folded into D. Gap/opening-auction behavior is the microstructure mechanism proposed to help explain family D's overnight/intraday split, not a separable return source with its own distinct test design; Block 5 already tested a dedicated 'Gap Continuation' variant on the current universe and it was REJECTED (§ETF_ROTATION_RESEARCH notes), so a fixed-gap-level strategy specifically is already known not to work here. D's own pre-registration (below) is the operative test for this mechanism.

families.name: Turn-of-month / calendar effects
families.economicRationaleOrigin: institutional (payroll-driven and pension/401(k) rebalancing flows concentrated at month-end/month-start) + structural
keyReferences: Lakonishok & Smidt (1988), "Are Seasonal Anomalies Real? A Ninety-Year Perspective", Review of Financial Studies
McConnell & Xu (2008), "Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month", Financial Analysts Journal
McLean & Pontiff (2016), "Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?", Journal of Finance
families.verdict: ADVANCED to Top-5 (#3), explicitly flagged HIGH decay risk per its own literature — see falsification design in the discovery report.

families.name: Earnings / post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: behavioral (underreaction to earnings surprise) + institutional (arbitrage now faster, per §27's decay questions)
keyReferences: Bernard & Thomas (1989), "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift", Journal of Accounting Research
Fink (2020), "A Review of the Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift", Borsa Istanbul Review / working paper survey
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced. Fink's own 2020 survey and the broader literature agree magnitude has shrunk materially since Bernard & Thomas as institutional participation increased (§27's decay question directly applies). More decisively for this project: PEAD requires a broad universe of individual stocks with point-in-time consensus-estimate data to avoid look-ahead — this project's current data sources (Yahoo, FRED) do not provide free, reliable, point-in-time analyst-estimate history, so this is DATA-classified UNAVAILABLE under this block's own no-fabrication rule (§12), not merely deprioritized.

families.name: Macro / rates conditioning
families.economicRationaleOrigin: risk premium (rate regime changes discount-rate the whole equity complex) + institutional
keyReferences: Gilchrist & Zakrajšek (2012), "Credit Spreads and Business Cycle Fluctuations", American Economic Review
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — merged with H above for this review (same data sources, same 40-variable-model risk the brief warns against). Not advanced this round.

families.name: Dispersion (index vol vs. constituent vol relative value)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: risk premium (implied correlation is itself priced) + institutional (index-option demand from structured products)
keyReferences: Driessen, Maenhout & Vilkov (2009), "The Price of Correlation Risk", Journal of Finance
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced. Requires simultaneous multi-name options positions (index + constituents) — a materially larger infrastructure and margin lift than single-name/single-index options, mostly practitioner- rather than academically-documented at retail scale, and not implementable on Alpaca today (single-underlying options only, no basket/correlation products). RESEARCH_ONLY, excluded for this round's scope.

families.name: Quality / value / momentum factors (standalone, beyond momentum already excluded)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: risk premium + behavioral (mispricing of quality/value characteristics)
keyReferences: Fama & French (1992/2015), "The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns" / "A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model", Journal of Finance / Journal of Financial Economics
Novy-Marx (2013), "The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium", Journal of Financial Economics
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — largely subsumed by F (defensive/low-vol, which can be implemented via a quality/low-vol ETF such as USMV/QUAL as the execution vehicle). Standalone value/quality investing on this project's 4-ETF universe isn't meaningful (SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA aren't individually 'value' or 'quality' names); a genuine factor-ETF rotation would need its own independence screen against RS3M and F before being worth a dedicated round. Not advanced this block.

families.name: Options-implied information (skew, put-call ratio as sentiment/positioning signals)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: information diffusion (informed traders often transact in options first) + behavioral (sentiment reflected in skew)
families.dataQuality: PARTIAL (needs options-chain snapshots, not just level data)
keyReferences: Bali & Hovakimian (2009), "Volatility Spreads and Expected Stock Returns", Management Science
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — not advanced as a standalone family this round; treated as a candidate SIGNAL ENHANCEMENT for E (volatility risk premium) in later rounds, not a separate 20-config budget item.

families.name: Futures-based index strategies (ES/NQ/RTY/YM structural advantages)
families.economicRationaleOrigin: structural (24h liquidity, capital efficiency, no ETF-creation friction)
families.expectedCorrelationWithRs3m: HIGH (same underlying indices, just a different wrapper)
keyReferences: CME Group, official E-mini/Micro E-mini index futures contract specifications (exchange documentation, not academic)
families.verdict: MAP ONLY — RESEARCH ONLY per §7.H's own instruction. Not a distinct return source (it trades the SAME underlying indices as RS3M/other families, just via a leveraged, margined, 24h-accessible instrument) — its value would be EXECUTION improvement for an already-selected family (e.g., running D's overnight strategy via ES instead of SPY to avoid pattern-day-trading/margin constraints), not a Top-5 slot of its own. Alpaca does not support futures; a futures broker is a prerequisite documented here, not built.

families.name: Other academically supported systematic anomalies
families.economicRationaleOrigin: n/a
families.verdict: No additional economically-distinct, evidence-backed family surfaced beyond A-S in this review. Per this block's own §17, ML/deep-learning/LLM/RL-discovered anomalies were explicitly excluded from this round's search (they may be investigated separately, later, under their own falsification-first mandate) — this is a deliberate scope boundary, not a finding that none exist.
